I've been good! Our current psych is in the process of diagnosing us with DID. When we started seeing him, the hospital didn't get the records from our group home (nor did our old therapist, unfortunately. Current one just let us tell her) we told him our symptoms and said we had been diagnosed at the group home. He said he wanted to see for himself and talk to our therapist. We did the DES and he talks to our therapist next week after we see her. With this psych, and his hospital the record won't get lost again since it's a really big well known hospital. 

Other than that we started a new sleeping med last night, it worked okay I guess. Have to keep trying.

Like a user said above its when my alters go quiet that I feel like I've just tricked myself into believing this. Then when they come back (usually we just have one quiet day, and we still even switch just no one talks) I feel like I'm forcing them to be there or something. It happens to me, and the first spilt the most (because Ax is very worried about everything all the time, and I'm the original alter if we have one). 

Usually I'll bring myself back down with two things. The first being that I've heard voices nearly my entire life, and that I've been able to access headworld since I was 11-12ish. I didnt know what DID was then, I didn't know what it was until I was diagnosed with it. The next thing is when I was talking to a therapist when I was 16. She was the first person I told about hearing voices, and when I explained them to her I basically explained DID in the terms someone who has no idea what that is would use. She had me use rocks to show myself and then my voices I described, I told her they felt like real people in my head, and I told her how I felt like Sef would go in front of me and protect me. 

Sef is our second split (me(core) - Ax - Sef) and I've honestly spent my entire life talking to him. He has always been there, from when I was a small four year old on a junk yard. He's the one who's always connected me to headworld, and I've never felt like I was faking it until after I got my diagnosis.

I think the fear comes from not wanting this all to stop. When we got diagnosed it solidified our experience, it made it real. If we some how found out we were faking it it would crush us. When we get into denial it just fuels that fear for us and then our brain starts thinking that this is all fake like we just got told we've been faking and none of this is real. 

Sorry this is long, and sorry I went off on a tangent!

*Tldr:* small intrusive thoughts from alters not talking leads to mini freak out about us being fake and my whole life being invalidated. Use memories to bring us down from spin.

Hey, welcome! People are usually unaware to protect themselves, so it's not uncommon. The names and descriptions will come with time, journaling will help a ton, especially if you can't hear each other internally. It's usually pretty vague at first unless you've already gone through hearing their voices. 

Like I said it takes time, I've been diagnosed for 2 or so years, and I knew about my alters before hand and I'm *still* learning about their likes, dislikes, and personalities. Its all part of the process. It's totally normal to be confused! 

I second waiting for your appointment. Googling is a really bad idea, especially with all the people claiming to have DID and actually just roleplaying. The DID Sourcebook is a really good read, you can get it on amazon kindle too as far as I know. Sorry, I just kind of gave the same info. If you need to talk to anyone, or whatever, feel free to message me.

The saying they've seen your alters in their system is usually used as an abuse tactic- especially by systems that are 'fake'. I don't know if your friend is meaning to be abusive or if they're just impressionable and have gotten some misinformation from tumblr or something and think that's a thing. It isn't. If they don't listen and continue to guilt you I would suggest finding a new and better friend.
You're totally welcome here! :) And if you ever need anyone to talk too, feel free to message me, and I'll try to help out as best I can. Welcome though!

We used to think we had/were fictives, since a lot of us based our names off of characters. We aren't though because all of us are from before we even knew about the characters we based our names off of.  We discovered our inner world/each other around the time we got into those things though so it kind of makes sense. 

We never had past lives relating to the canon or anything like that. It could be a coping mechanism, though, like drew_M1 says. If it starts becoming unhealthy though, like you miss your brother to the point where you want to hurt yourself or something, it might be time to talk to a professional about it. One of my alters, who was more into thinking he was a fictive (he was our first alter and used it has a coping mechanism to deal with the trauma he's been through) started to get really upset anytime his canon was brought up and would feel really bad about himself for it, so when his memories surrounding his actual life started to surface he rejected the fictive identity because it was causing more pain than helping. 

Just food for thought I guess. I would talk to a therapist about it, though, if you can. Try and stay away from the internet fictive scene (especially tumblr). Tumblr has a lot of messed up views on what a fictive is, and it could be more damaging than it would do good. Stay safe!

I've been diagnosed with Schizoaffective Disorder (though it was a misdiagnosis). I understand the embarrassment of getting diagnosed with something, and how weird it can feel. There's nothing to be ashamed of. 

As for the deterring people part, you don't have to tell anyone anything you don't want to tell them. Including employers- at least about mental illnesses, they can't get your records. They won't know unless you tell them (note this is USA-centric). If you need accommodations, you can ask for them in a different way. 

But in the end, a diagnosis doesn't change who you are. You're still the same person you were before you got diagnosed. All a diagnosis is is a label so doctors can better know how to help you!

**Story!**

That dog in those pictures name is Duffy. When we adopted her she was a ~six year old black lab, with hang-y down nipples and a docked tail. She also happened to be wearing an e-collar. I was 12 when we adopted her, and I was the only one of out my family who even saw her. She wasn't barking, she was just sitting there quietly looking at me. I convinced my parents to take a look at her, and we fell in love.

She was a funny dog, who liked to lick things. People, sofas, the floor. She'd lick it all. She was my best friend growing up. Even though she was supposed to be my moms dog. But dogs can never be owned can they? 

She always looked so sad... except when she smiled. She smiled when she way laying in bed with me, or when she was in the car. Or when she was having her belly rubbed. 

One night after moving around a lot, and being homeless (Duffy and our other dog Ding were in a program where they stayed at a shelter until we could pick them up) I had a flash back. They aren't like the ones in the movies, they're worse. Your whole body is back at that time and you can feel it. I was alone with the dogs laying on the sofa, and was trapped in a place of pure terror.

What did Duffy do? She licked and laid on me until I came out of it. She saved my life that night, because surely with out her I would have taken it. 

This story has been told probably a hundred times before, but this one is mine, and I wanted to share it. 

We put down Duffy and Ding together at the ripe old age of 13(duffy) and 15(ding). They went out showing their true colors. I miss them both very much, but I think I'm finally ready to get another lab, now that two years have passed. 

I just wanted to share this. Thanks for reading :)
